editorial:
Imagine moving into a huge, old house only to find a creepy, life-sized doll left behind for your kid to play with. That is exactly what happens here. You get to follow a family that thinks they found a great deal on a mansion, but things get weird fast. The kid starts talking to the doll, Brahms, as if it is a real person. You will feel that uneasy tension as the parents realize something is hiding in the walls and watching their every move. It is a slow burn that builds up a lot of stress before the scary stuff really kicks in.

The acting is solid and the twists keep you guessing until the end. While some parts might feel a bit slow, the payoff is worth it for anyone who likes a good mystery. If you love jump scares and creepy dolls, you should definitely give this a go. For the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the dark corners of the house. If you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great way to keep this spooky ride forever.
endingExplained: You find out that Brahms is not a ghost, but a grown man who has been living inside the walls of the house for years. He becomes obsessed with the young boy and tries to keep him. In the final fight, the mother fights back to save her son. She eventually kills the man, ending his reign of terror. The movie wraps up with the family finally safe and the mystery of the doll solved.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves creepy dolls and home invasion stories.
